Module 3 — The Verifier’s Toolkit
Effective verification is not about using a single tool — it is about knowing which tools to use, when to use them, and how to combine them within structured newsroom workflows.

This module introduces the practical toolkit of modern digital verification and explains how journalists can apply verification technologies across different reporting scenarios. Learners explore reverse image search systems, metadata analysis, geolocation techniques, verification decision trees, and AI-assisted workflows while developing a systematic approach to digital investigation and evidence evaluation.

Rather than presenting tools in isolation, the module focuses on verification logic, workflow integration, and practical newsroom application.
1
Tool‑Selection Decision Tree
This interactive decision tree guides learners through a series of questions about their verification task: content type (image, video, text, audio), file availability (original or screenshot), and verification goal (find source, detect manipulation, geolocate, identify objects). Based on the answers, the tool recommends the most appropriate verification tools (e.g., reverse image search, InVID, metadata extractors).
Learning outcome: Learners understand how to choose the right tool for a specific scenario, rather than using tools randomly.
Tool‑selection decision tree | Module 3

🌲 Tool‑selection decision tree

Answer a few questions to find the right verification tool for your scenario.
2
Interactive Verification Workflow Maps
Learners can select between three common verification scenarios (image, video, or text/claim). For each scenario, a step‑by‑step workflow map is displayed, listing the logical sequence of actions (e.g., extract metadata → reverse image search → geolocation) and the recommended tools for each step. The map is interactive: clicking on different scenarios changes the workflow displayed.
Learning outcome: Learners see how individual tools fit together into a complete verification workflow, and understand the order of operations for efficient fact‑checking.
Verification workflow maps | Module 3

🗺️ Interactive verification workflow maps

Select a verification scenario to see the recommended workflow steps and tools.

Modern journalism operates in rapidly changing digital environments where manipulated visuals, misleading claims, and synthetic media circulate across platforms within seconds.

This module helps learners move beyond isolated tools and develop a structured verification workflow mindset that supports efficient, transparent, and responsible newsroom verification practices.
3
“Choose The Right Tool” Quiz
A short multiple‑choice quiz that tests learners’ ability to match a verification task with the correct tool. Four realistic scenarios are presented (e.g., “find the earliest appearance of a photo”, “extract frames from a video”, “check if a quote was fact‑checked”). Learners select one tool from four options. After submission, they receive a score and feedback explaining the correct choice.
Learning outcome: Reinforces tool‑selection logic and helps learners memorise which tool to use for which type of verification problem.
Choose the right tool quiz | Module 3

📝 “Choose the right tool” quiz

Select the best verification tool for each scenario.

4
Guided Tool Demonstrations
This section provides step‑by‑step instructions for four essential verification tools: reverse image search, InVID/WeVerify plugin, geolocation basics, and metadata extraction. Learners click on a tool name, and a card appears with numbered steps and a practical note. No external videos are needed – the instructions are written and can be followed directly.
Learning outcome: Learners gain hands‑on procedural knowledge of how to use key verification tools, even without watching external tutorials.
Guided tool demonstrations | Module 3

🛠️ Guided tool demonstrations

Click on a tool to see step‑by‑step instructions.

5
Verification Checklist Downloads
Three ready‑to‑use checklists (for image, video, and text verification) are presented as cards. Each checklist contains the key actions in a simple bullet‑point format. Learners can copy the checklist to their clipboard with one click, then paste it into their own notes, newsroom wiki, or task manager. A short toast notification confirms the copy action.
Learning outcome: Learners walk away with practical, reusable resources that can be integrated into their daily verification routines and shared with colleagues.
After completing this module, learners will develop a practical understanding of how verification tools, workflows, and decision-making processes interact within modern digital journalism and AI-assisted verification environments.
Verification checklist downloads | Module 3

📋 Verification checklist downloads

Copy the checklist text or save it for your newsroom workflow.

📸 Image verification checklist
  • ☐ Extract EXIF metadata (date, camera, GPS)
  • ☐ Run reverse image search (Google, Yandex, TinEye)
  • ☐ Perform error level analysis (FotoForensics)
  • ☐ Check for image manipulation (cloning, splicing)
  • ☐ Geolocate using visible landmarks
  • ☐ Cross‑reference with trusted news archives
🎥 Video verification checklist
  • ☐ Extract keyframes (InVID/WeVerify, FFmpeg)
  • ☐ Reverse image search on keyframes
  • ☐ Check video metadata (MediaInfo)
  • ☐ Analyze audio for synthetic voice (spectrogram)
  • ☐ Look for deepfake artifacts (inconsistent blinking, lip sync)
  • ☐ Geolocate using street signs, architecture, weather
📄 Text / claim verification checklist
  • ☐ Identify the core claim (check‑worthy)
  • ☐ Search fact‑check databases (Google Fact Check Explorer)
  • ☐ Find original source / full context
  • ☐ Verify author credibility (domain age, social history)
  • ☐ Check for AI‑generated text (GPTZero, Copyleaks)
  • ☐ Cross‑reference multiple independent sources
✅ Copied to clipboard!
